title: Assess platform, data, and distributed-system trust boundaries: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: Which client, server, data, distributed, or management boundary must enforce this decision?
focalInsight: Authoritative server-side and management-plane controls must constrain every high-impact path.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Client Security
nodes.definition: Protection of endpoint execution, local data, credentials, patch state, and user interaction.
nodes.detail: Protection of endpoint execution, local data, credentials, patch state, and user interaction.
nodes.decision: Choose endpoint management, anti-malware, updates, local-data protection, and network controls by exposure.
nodes.failureExample: A stolen thick client retains sensitive files and malware pivots to a server.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Client risk includes local compromise and a path into connected systems.

nodes.label: Server Security
nodes.definition: Protection of centrally managed service systems, their privileged administration, and support paths.
nodes.detail: Protection of centrally managed service systems, their privileged administration, and support paths.
nodes.decision: Assess patchability, redundancy, physical/logistics access, monitoring volume, and service role.
nodes.failureExample: An unsupported server stays unpatched because no redundant maintenance window exists.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Server availability design can remove the reason to defer critical patches.

nodes.label: Database Security
nodes.definition: Protection of database data, DBMS interfaces, service identities, backups, and administrator paths.
nodes.detail: Protection of database data, DBMS interfaces, service identities, backups, and administrator paths.
nodes.decision: Control authorization, queries, input, replication, backups, logs, and separation of duties.
nodes.failureExample: A malformed query bypasses controls on high-value records.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Database security covers data paths and privilege paths.

nodes.label: Cryptographic System
nodes.definition: System of algorithms, keys, protocols, trust validation, and recovery dependencies.
nodes.detail: System of algorithms, keys, protocols, trust validation, and recovery dependencies.
nodes.decision: Select proven solutions by data state, performance, key distribution, trust, and endpoint assumptions.
nodes.failureExample: A team invents encryption and leaves its bulk-encryption key distribution exposed.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Use well-tested crypto and design the key and recovery system.

nodes.label: Distributed System
nodes.definition: Cooperating nodes that exchange identity, state, time, and work across imperfect networks.
nodes.detail: Cooperating nodes that exchange identity, state, time, and work across imperfect networks.
nodes.decision: Plan for partial failure, replay, inconsistent state, dependency loss, and observability.
nodes.failureExample: A retry after timeout repeats an authorization-sensitive transaction.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Distributed failure behavior is a security design condition.

nodes.label: Trust Boundary
nodes.definition: Point where a different actor, privilege, data classification, or control assumption begins.
nodes.detail: Point where a different actor, privilege, data classification, or control assumption begins.
nodes.decision: Identify boundary crossings before granting access or accepting data.
nodes.failureExample: An application treats a browser-supplied role as trustworthy.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A boundary needs validation and an authoritative decision.

nodes.label: Management Plane
nodes.definition: Privileged interfaces and workflows used to configure or administer systems.
nodes.detail: Privileged interfaces and workflows used to configure or administer systems.
nodes.decision: Protect with strong attributable authentication, segmentation, least privilege, logs, and review.
nodes.failureExample: One console edits production guests, templates, and virtual switches.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Management authority can have a larger blast radius than a workload.

nodes.label: Segmentation
nodes.definition: Policy-enforced separation that limits unwanted communication across zones.
nodes.detail: Policy-enforced separation that limits unwanted communication across zones.
nodes.decision: Use when client, server, management, database, or tenant paths need distinct reachability.
nodes.failureExample: A compromised client reaches the database management port directly.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Segment both the workload path and the privileged path.

nodes.label: Service Account Management
nodes.definition: Creation, scoping, rotation, attribution, and review of nonhuman service identities.
nodes.detail: Creation, scoping, rotation, attribution, and review of nonhuman service identities.
nodes.decision: Give each service only needed permissions and avoid shared broad credentials.
nodes.failureExample: All APIs use one unrestricted database account.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Service accounts need least privilege and accountability too.
